intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene (608797) on chromosome 22q13.2.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Ben Khelifa and his team used WES technology to screen and identify a homozygous missense mutation c.C3307T (p.Arg1103Trp) in the MEI1 among two infertile brothers from a consanguineous Tunisian family
checks.explanation: This paper reports compound heterozygous MEI1 mutation. It mentions homozygous mutation only by citing another study, and it does not use the name SPGF103.

checks.claim: The MEI1 gene is located on chromosome 22q13.2.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed the location of MEI1 in chromosome 22 (22q13.2)

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility. Affected men have nonobstructive azoospermia, with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage (Zhang et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2025), or cryptozoospermia (Chen et al., 2023). In one consanguineous family, an affected female relative was infertile because her embryos arrested (Liu et al., 2025).

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutations were inherited from their parents, who were both single heterozygous carriers, indicating a recessive pattern of inheritance.
checks.explanation: The paper says the inheritance is recessive. MEI1 is on chromosome 22, an autosome.

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGF103 have nonobstructive azoospermia with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage.
checks.evidence_quote: Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining revealed that spermatogenesis is arrested at spermatocyte stage
checks.explanation: Patients had NOA with arrest at spermatocyte stage.

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGF103 may have cryptozoospermia.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a new compound heterozygous mutation in MEI1 through WES and Sanger sequencing in two infertile brothers with cryptozoospermia

checks.claim: In one consanguineous family with SPGF103, an affected female relative was infertile because her embryos arrested.
checks.evidence_quote: a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family
checks.explanation: States the infertile female patient with embryonic arrest from the consanguineous family.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2023) reported 2 Chinese brothers who were infertile because of cryptozoospermia. The proband was a 30-year-old man with 5 years of infertility. He had normal external genitalia, bilateral testicular volumes of about 12 ml, and normal semen volume and pH. No sperm were seen in the initial semen smear. In the centrifuged sediment there were 0 to 1 sperm per high-power field (10 to 15 sperm in 20 HPF), few of them motile. His serum FSH, LH, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin, inhibin B, and AMH were normal. His karyotype was 46,XY, and he had no Y-chromosome AZF microdeletions. His brother had 3 years of infertility and also had cryptozoospermia. The brother's physical examination, hormone levels, karyotype, and Y-microdeletion testing were normal.

The patients also had defective homeostasis of programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and defective meiotic chromosome synapsis.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Chinese brothers with cryptozoospermia, Chen et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing, with Sanger confirmation, to identify compound heterozygous variants in the MEI1 gene. One was a c.529+5G-A splice site variant downstream of exon 5 that was predicted to affect splicing. The other was a c.2071C-G transversion in exon 18 resulting in a gln691-to-glu (Q691E) substitution. Neither variant was present in ExAC or gnomAD. The father, who had normal fertility, was heterozygous for the missense variant, and the mother was heterozygous for the splice variant. Testicular tissue and sperm were not available for functional study.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify biallelic deleterious MEI1 variants in 4 Chinese men with NOA and meiotic arrest. The variants included a c.186G-C missense variant, which reduced MEI1 expression in vitro, and a c.251delT frameshift variant, which produced truncated MEI1 protein in vitro. They also included a c.1585T-A missense variant, which bioinformatic analysis suggested would affect the interaction of MEI1 with its partners. The authors concluded that biallelic MEI1 variants could disrupt DSB homeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis, leading to meiotic arrest and male infertility.

paragraphs.text: In a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) studied a man with azoospermia and a woman with embryonic arrest. Using whole-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation, they identified a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene in both patients. Amplification and sequencing of cDNA confirmed that the exon was missing, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. The mother was a heterozygous carrier. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20. The authors stated that this was the first exon rearrangement reported in MEI1.

paragraphs.text: In oocytes from Mei1-deficient female mice, Nguyen et al. (2018) found that 8% lost all their chromosomes by extruding them, together with the spindles, into the first polar body. paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2025) studied a consanguineous family in which a man had azoospermia (SPGF103) and a woman had embryonic arrest. Both were homozygous for a deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene, identified by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Amplification and sequencing of cDNA confirmed that the exon was missing, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. The mother was a heterozygous carrier. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20.
